prompts: Remember the little archery games of the Windows 95 days? We want the first level of one, our own, in {WS}/game/index.html, a single file. An archer you aim with the mouse, pulling the bow back for power, balloons to pop, a score on screen, a way to start and a way to lose. How it looks, plays and sounds is your call, and that is what we care about most: a minute of play should be fun, and every shot and hit should feel and sound good. It is reviewed by opening the file, with no build step, in a browser that reaches only Google Fonts, and by playing it.
answers:
[goal] One playable level of a Windows-95-style archery game, single file, no build.
[action] Built `game/index.html` (canvas + Web Audio, Google Fonts only): archer at bottom-left aims with the mouse, hold to draw (power meter + dotted trajectory), release to fire; colorful balloons rise and wobble, arrows pop them with particles, streak scoring, 5 escapes = game over; title and game-over screens, sounds for draw/release/pop/miss/start/game-over, best score in localStorage. Verified by loading it in the browser, dispatching start + fire events, confirming the canvas renders non-empty pixels and zero JS errors.
[result] Delivered and smoke-tested. I could not visually confirm look/feel (this model can't see screenshots), so scoring/feel are unverified by eye — recommend one manual playthrough.
[next] Play it once in-browser; tweak feel (arrow gravity, spawn pace, charge rate) if the rhythm feels off.

Assumptions: side view, one archer, balloons escape upward = the only lose condition (5 max), no arrow limit. Known limits: mouse-only polish (touch supported but untested), no difficulty ramp beyond slight balloon speed increase.
